messages:
Anna (support): Medilink just flagged missing KMS "Decrypt" audit entries for their dedicated cluster in eu-west-2. They sent a sample time window and say apps showed 4 decrypts but our audit logs show none. Can sec-eng oncall take a look? :eyes:
Jay (sec-eng): Looking. Can you paste the sample window and the customer tenant id?
Anna (support): Tenant medilink-42, window 2026-02-12 14:02:00 - 14:12:00 UTC. They attached app logs showing calls to kms.decrypt with request IDs.
Tom (sre): I'm going to check the audit-forwarder and filebeat on their dedicated nodes. Quick question: are we certain Dedicated uses the same audit pipeline as Hosted? (IIRC we have a separate logshipper config)
Jay (sec-eng): Right, dedicated clusters route to a tenant-scoped pipeline. Common failure modes: rsyslog rotation, filebeat backpressure, or KMS audit plugin misconfig. I'll grep for the request IDs in the raw S3 bucket first.
Anna (support): Customer is asking for an ETA; they say this impacts compliance reporting. Leah (cust-success) is on the call with them.
Leah (cust-success): Yep, I'm with the customer. They're pretty concerned, want confirmation if keys were used and if any data exfil. Please triage fast.
Tom (sre): Ran quick check: filebeat for medilink-42 shows a 5 min gap at 14:04 where queue size spiked. agent logs: "publish failed: backoff/queue overflow". Attaching tail of filebeat.log:
```
2026-02-12T14:04:02Z INFO queue.go:312 publish failed: write tcp 10.3.4.2:50123->10.9.9.10:5044: write: broken pipe
2026-02-12T14:04:03Z WARN registrar.go:92 registry file rotated unexpectedly
```
Jay (sec-eng): That's interesting. If filebeat dropped events during rotation, KMS audit plugin could have logged locally but not forwarded. Can you check node-local /var/log/kms_audit.log and the agent path for that window?
Tom (sre): Mounting into medilink node now, grabbing grep output. Found kms_audit.log entries for decrypts at 14:03:58 and 14:05:11. So plugin did emit events. They just weren't forwarded.
Anna (support): OK so events exist on node-local. Customer wants export of those entries. Any privacy concerns about pulling node-local logs into support bundle?
Jay (sec-eng): It's fine under the dedicated contract; we need to sanitize any customer payloads when sharing. Export only the audit metadata: request-id, key-id, principal, timestamp, action. Do not include plaintext inputs.
Leah (cust-success): I'll tell them we'll provide signed excerpts and a timeline within the hour.
Tom (sre): Continuing root cause: filebeat config had stale multiline settings plus rsyslog rotated registry file due to aggressive rotation setting (rotate 1). That caused file offsets to reset and Filebeat treated files as new, but the filebeat registry corruption caused a short drop.
Jay (sec-eng): Actionable items: 1) reingest node-local logs for medilink-42 into the audit index for that window (owner: Tom). 2) Provide sanitized export to customer (owner: Leah). 3) Add alert rule for filebeat queue/backpressure per-tenant (owner: Jay). 4) Postmortem and config change: rsyslog rotation default -> rotate 7 (owner: infra team).
Tom (sre): Kicking off reingest job: script I'm running:
```
aws s3 cp /var/log/medilink/ks_audit_20260212.gz s3://redwood-dedicated-raw/medilink-42/ || true
python infra/tools/reingest_audit.py --tenant medilink-42 --start '2026-02-12T14:00:00Z' --end '2026-02-12T14:15:00Z'
```
Jay (sec-eng): Confirm reingest began at 14:27 UTC. Monitor for duplicates; dedupe logic should handle it but watch index size.
Anna (support): Customer update: they asked if keys were compromised. Can we confirm decrypt principal is an internal ARN and not an unknown principal?
Jay (sec-eng): From the node logs I grep'd, principal=arn:redwood:service:dedicated/medilink-42:server-agent. No unknown principals. Send that to customer with assurance.
Leah (cust-success): Drafting msg to customer now. Will include sanitized table and note that audit events were delayed due to log forwarder gap; no evidence of external access. ETA sending in 25m.
Tom (sre): Reingest completed at 14:41 UTC. Entries are visible in ES and mapped to original request IDs. Running a quick query to validate counts match app logs.
Jay (sec-eng): I've created a temporary dashboard and a Kibana query. Counts match 4 decrypts in that window. Created ticket SEC-INC-2026-021 with summary and assigned to infra for rotation config change.
Anna (support): Customer notified and pleased with promptness. They requested a follow-up doc describing mitigations and a timeline.
Leah (cust-success): I'll own the customer follow-up doc and coordinate exec summary. Jay/Tom, can you attach the tech appendix with logs and remediation steps by EOD?
Tom (sre): Yep will drop appendix into the ticket. Also adding a one-line runbook entry: "If filebeat queue > 80% for 1m, page SRE oncall and throttle ingest." 
Jay (sec-eng): Post-incident actions: create alert, push rsyslog rotation change to dedicated node image, add unit test in filebeat packaging to prevent registry corruption, and schedule a 1-week follow-up to ensure no regressions.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident SEC-INC-2026-021 acknowledged by Jay (sec-eng) at 2026-02-12T15:02:00Z
Anna (support): Closing thread after EOD attachments posted. Thanks all :lock:
